59640-the-tenants-an-episode-of-the-80s:
Mary S Watts wrote a novel published by McClure at New York in March 1908, called an episode of the eighties. They were tearing down the old Gwynne house the other day, the narrator begins, as we drove past. It was not without sentimental regret that they beheld the spectacle. The newspapers honored the house as an historic landmark.

The tenants of the title occupy that house in the remembered decade. Watts wrote of Cincinnati society and its changes. Her episode looks back twenty years at manners already vanishing. McClure published several of her novels. The demolition frame lets the past be entered like a house.

Danny Jones hosts a talk built around Andy Puharich and a claimed deathbed confession by a CIA-linked scientist. The episode title says new files expose contact with aliens. Puharich was a doctor and researcher tied to mind studies and strange claims.

The talk works through the files and the confession as the show presents them. It asks who the scientist was, what he claimed to know, and why the story stayed buried. Jones keeps the focus on what the papers say and where they came from. Listeners who track UFO lore will find a deep cut here. The library holds the episode as an archive record.
